extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: A modifier is a two-character code appended to a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code or Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code to clarify the services rendered without changing the procedure code. Modifiers can facilitate editing, increase accuracy in reimbursement and improve coding consistency. Documentation of services must support a submitted modifier.

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana plans require the use of CPT and HCPCS modifiers when appropriate. If a modifier is submitted, the claim is subject to review to ensure the procedure code and modifier combination is correct and the modifier was necessary. If modifiers are submitted inappropriately, the claim line is denied or payment recovery will occur. Below is a list of some commonly used modifiers, a high-level explanation of how those modifiers are generally used for reimbursement and general reporting information.
